   589	    async def _research_mail(self, kinds: list, deadline: float | None = None, starts: list | None = None) -> None:
   590	        """
   591	        Search the record kinds over the mail tabs (one kind per tab at a time) until the mail deadline, then
   592	        resolve whatever records were read: a kind still open at the deadline is dropped, the rest go to calc.
   593	        Results accumulate, so a rework of some kinds keeps the others. `starts` are tabs still signing in; each
   594	        joins as soon as it is ready (a tab that never opens just leaves the work to the others).
   595	        """
   596	        queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
   597	        # The approval goes first: the discount counts for points of its own and feeds every unit price. The
   598	        # stroke reserves and the condition rules follow: materials (and so most positions) and the discount
   599	        # scopes wait on them.
   600	        first = ("approval", "end_reserves", "condition_rules")
   601	        for kind in sorted(kinds, key=lambda k: first.index(k.name) if k.name in first else len(first)):
   602	            queue.put_nowait((kind, 0))
   603	        deadline = deadline or self.mail_deadline
   604	
   605	        address: list[asyncio.Task] = []
   606	
   607	        async def tab(source) -> None:
   608	            if isinstance(source, SiteSession):
   609	                session = source
   610	            else:
   611	                try:
   612	                    session = await source
   613	                except Exception:
   614	                    return
   615	                self.mail_sessions.append(session)
   616	            if not address:  # the first open tab also looks up the mailbox address, alongside its searches
   617	                address.append(asyncio.create_task(self._mailbox()))
   618	            while not queue.empty() and time.monotonic() < deadline - 20:
   619	                kind, tries = queue.get_nowait()
   620	                try:
   621	                    budget = self._kind_seconds(deadline, queue.qsize())
   622	                    options = {"seconds": budget} if "seconds" in KIND_OPTIONS else {}
   623	                    found = await research_mail.research_kind(session, kind, self.reference, deadline=deadline,
   624	                                                               **options)
   625	                except Exception as error:  # one failed kind must not cost the others
   626	                    self.board.problem("mails", f"{kind.name}: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
   627	                    continue
   628	                earlier = self.mail_results.get(kind.name)
   629	                if earlier is not None:  # a second try adds to what the first one read
   630	                    found.records = [*earlier.records, *found.records]
   631	                    found.kept = [*earlier.kept, *found.kept]
   632	                self.mail_results[kind.name] = found
   633	                stopped = getattr(found, "stopped", None)
   634	                if stopped is None:  # out of its budget without reading a message
   635	                    stopped = not found.records and found.seconds >= min(budget, getattr(research_mail, "KIND_SECONDS", budget)) - 5
   636	                if (stopped and not tries
   637	                        and deadline - time.monotonic() > MAIL_RETRY_SECONDS):
   638	                    # Out of its budget: once more at the end of the queue, from a fresh start on this tab.
   639	                    self.board.problem("mails", f"{kind.name}: search stopped at its budget; tried once more")
   640	                    queue.put_nowait((kind, 1))
   641	
   642	        tabs = [asyncio.create_task(tab(s)) for s in (starts or list(self.mail_sessions))]
   643	        _, late = await asyncio.wait(tabs, timeout=max(1.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
   644	        for job in late:
   645	            job.cancel()
   646	        for start in starts or []:
   647	            if not start.done():
   648	                start.cancel()
   649	        if late:
   650	            await asyncio.gather(*late, return_exceptions=True)
   651	        open_kinds = [k.name for k in kinds if k.name not in self.mail_results]
   652	        if open_kinds:
   653	            self.board.problem("mails", f"mail deadline: {open_kinds} not read; their fields stay blank")
   654	        if not self.mail_sessions:
   655	            raise ConnectionError("no mail tab could be opened")
   656	        mailbox = await address[0] if address else await self._mailbox()
   657	        facts = research_mail.resolve_mail(list(self.mail_results.values()), self.reference,
   658	                                           mailbox.split("@", 1)[1] if "@" in mailbox else "", self.scenario, mailbox)
   659	        if not mailbox:
   660	            facts.problems.append("mailbox address not found: no sender could be authorised")
   661	        for problem in facts.problems:
   662	            self.board.problem("mails", problem)
   663	        self.mail_facts = facts
   664	        site = self.mail_sessions[0].site["siteId"].split(":")[0]
   665	        used = {}
   666	        for s in getattr(facts, "sources", []):
   667	            if s.used:
   668	                used.setdefault(s.kind, []).append(f"{s.subject} | {s.sender} | {s.sent_at.isoformat()} | {s.reference}")
   669	        def post(kind: str, key: str, value) -> None:
   670	            self.board.post("mail", f"{kind}/{key}", value if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, dict, list))
   671	                            else value.model_dump(mode="json") if hasattr(value, "model_dump") else str(value),
   672	                            Source(site=site, quote="; ".join(used.get(kind, [])) or "(no record used)"), "mails")
   673	        if facts.approval is not None:
   674	            post("approval", "latest", facts.approval)
   675	        for table, kind in (("discount_scopes", "condition_rules"), ("metal_indices", "metal_indices"),
   676	                            ("end_reserves", "end_reserves"), ("packaging", "packaging"),
   677	                            ("commitments", "commitments"), ("fx_rates", "fx"), ("setup_pools", "setup_pools"),
   678	                            ("project_bonuses", "project_bonus")):
   679	            for key, value in (getattr(facts, table, None) or {}).items():
   680	                post(kind, key, [v.model_dump(mode="json") for v in value] if isinstance(value, list) else value)

   687	        sites: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # a role may be spread over several websites in another dataset
   688	        for n in self.plan.needs:
   689	            if n.site not in sites.setdefault(n.kind, []):
   690	                sites[n.kind].append(n.site)
   691	        jobs = []
   692	        if "tender" in sites and research_tender is not None:
   693	            jobs += [asyncio.create_task(self.tender(site), name=f"tender@{site}") for site in sites["tender"]]
   694	        elif "tender" in sites:
   695	            self.board.problem("plan", "tender research module not available")
   696	        erp_sites = sites.get("materials", [])
   697	        if len(erp_sites) > 1:
   698	            self.board.problem("plan", f"materials on several sites {erp_sites}; only the first is searched")
   699	        for site in sites.get("specification", []):
   700	            jobs.append(asyncio.create_task(self.specification(site, erp_sites[0] if erp_sites else None),

   702	        if "mails" in sites and research_mail is not None:
   703	            jobs += [asyncio.create_task(self.mails(site), name=f"mails@{site}") for site in sites["mails"]]
   704	        elif "mails" in sites:
   705	            self.board.problem("plan", "mail research module not available")
   706	        if not jobs:
   707	            return
   708	        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(jobs, timeout=max(1.0, self.left()))
   709	        for job in pending:  # the deadline guard: whatever is complete goes on
   710	            job.cancel()
   711	            self.board.problem("deadline", f"{job.get_name()} stopped at the research deadline")
   712	        if pending:
   713	            await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
   714	        if self._erp is not None:  # ERP workers still browsing would compete with the bid form for the browser
   715	            for task in [*self._erp.tasks.values(), *self._erp.materials.values()]:
   716	                if not task.done():
   717	                    task.cancel()
   718	            if self.erp is None:  # stopped at the deadline: what finished still counts
   719	                so_far = getattr(self._erp, "so_far", None)
   720	                self.erp = so_far() if so_far is not None else self._finished_erp()
   721	        self.rework = {"mails": self._rework_mail}
   722	
   723	    def _finished_erp(self) -> ErpResearch:
   724	        def finished(tasks):
   725	            return {k: t.result() for k, t in tasks.items()
   726	                    if t.done() and not t.cancelled() and t.exception() is None and t.result() is not None}
   727	        return ErpResearch(requirements=list(finished(self._erp.tasks).values()),
   728	                           materials=finished(self._erp.materials))
   729	
   730	    async def _rework_mail(self, doubtful: list) -> None:
   731	        names = {f.key.split("/")[0] for f in doubtful}
   732	        kinds = [k for k in self.mail_kinds if k.name in names]
   733	        if kinds and self.mail_sessions:
   734	            await self._research_mail(kinds, min(self.research_deadline, time.monotonic() + REWORK_SECONDS))
   735	
   736	    async def verify(self) -> None:
   737	        doubtful = await verify_board(self.board, self.rules, self.reference, self.briefing.scenario_date)
   738	        by_worker: dict[str, list] = {}
   739	        for fact in doubtful:
   740	            by_worker.setdefault(fact.worker, []).append(fact)
   741	        for worker, facts in by_worker.items():
   742	            rework = self.rework.get(worker)
   743	            if rework is None or self.left() < REWORK_SECONDS:
   744	                continue
   745	            self.trace.event("verify", "rework", by=worker, facts=[f.ident for f in facts])
   746	            try:
   747	                await asyncio.wait_for(rework(facts), max(1.0, self.left()))
   748	            except Exception as error:
   749	                self.board.problem("verify", f"rework {worker}: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
   750	        if by_worker:
   751	            await verify_board(self.board, self.rules, self.reference, self.briefing.scenario_date)
   752	
   753	    async def select_materials(self) -> None:
   754	        """The final material choice, once amendments and reserves are on the board (reselect: no browsing)."""
   755	        if self.erp is None or not self.requirements:
   756	            return
   757	        effective = [self.effective(req) for req in self.requirements.values()]
   758	        own = {r.requirement_id: r.selected for r in self.erp.requirements}
   759	        # One choice per requirement, side by side: one hung model call must not cost the others; choices not made
   760	        # in time are the ERP workers' own.
   761	        tasks = {req.requirement_id: asyncio.create_task(reselect([req], self.erp, self.trace)) for req in effective}
   762	        _, late_tasks = await asyncio.wait(tasks.values(), timeout=SELECT_SECONDS)
   763	        for task in late_tasks:
   764	            task.cancel()
   765	        if late_tasks:
   766	            await asyncio.gather(*late_tasks, return_exceptions=True)
   767	        chosen = {}
   768	        for rid, task in tasks.items():
   769	            if task.done() and not task.cancelled() and task.exception() is None:
   770	                chosen.update(task.result())
   771	        late = sorted(set(own) - set(chosen))
   772	        if late:
   773	            self.board.problem("select", f"no new choice in time for {late}; the ERP workers' choices are used")
   774	        self.chosen = {**own, **chosen}
   775	        self.trace.event("select", "done", chosen=self.chosen)
   776	
   777	    def _unknown_clauses(self, p, clause, pool, bonus) -> None:
   778	        """A position whose Q&A names a key the mails did not resolve: calc would report a zero for that part,
   779	        which reads as a known zero, so the report field and the unit price it feeds are left blank instead."""
   780	        fields = set()
   781	        if getattr(p, "packaging_key", None) and getattr(clause, "packaging", None) is None:
   782	            fields |= {"packaging_per_unit", "unit_price"}
   783	        if getattr(p, "setup_pool_key", None) and p.position not in getattr(pool, "members", []):
   784	            fields |= {"surcharge_per_unit", "unit_price"}
   785	        if getattr(p, "bonus_key", None) and p.position not in getattr(bonus, "members", []):
   786	            fields |= {"rebate_total", "unit_price"}
   787	        if fields:
   788	            self.blank_hints.setdefault(p.position, set()).update(fields)
   789	
   790	    def build_bid(self) -> tuple[calc.BidInput, list[str]]:
   791	        self.blank_hints = {}
   792	        self.attributes = {}
   793	        problems: list[str] = []
   794	        clauses = None
   795	        if self.tender_facts is not None and self.mail_facts is not None and research_mail is not None:
   796	            try:
   797	                clauses = research_mail.bid_clauses(self.tender_facts, self.mail_facts)
   798	                problems += list(clauses.problems)
   799	            except Exception as error:
   800	                problems.append(f"bid clauses: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
   801	        by_position = {c.position: c for c in getattr(clauses, "positions", [])}
   802	        positions = []
   803	        for p in getattr(self.tender_facts, "positions", []) or []:
   804	            req_id = next((rid for rid in self.requirements if _same_id(rid, p.requirement)), None)
   805	            if req_id is None:
   806	                problems.append(f"position {p.position}: requirement {p.requirement} not read; position omitted")
   807	                continue
   808	            research = next((r for r in (self.erp.requirements if self.erp else []) if r.requirement_id == req_id),
   809	                            None)
   810	            # without a final choice (reselect cut short) the ERP worker's own choice stands
   811	            number = self.chosen[req_id] if req_id in self.chosen else getattr(research, "selected", None)
   812	            if number is None and (research is None or not research.inspected):
   813	                problems.append(f"position {p.position}: ERP not researched; position omitted")
   814	                continue
   815	            if number is None:
   816	                # No material only means no_bid (rule 3) when the search for it was complete; a requirement still
   817	                # pending (e.g. a reserve not found) or a search that hit problems leaves the position out instead.
   818	                pending = self.effective(self.requirements[req_id]).pending
   819	                if pending or (research is not None and research.problems):
   820	                    problems.append(f"position {p.position}: material undecided "
   821	                                    f"({'; '.join(pending or research.problems)[:160]}); position omitted")
   822	                    continue
   823	            material = self.erp.materials.get(number) if (number and self.erp) else None
   824	            if material is not None:
   825	                self.attributes[p.position] = material_attributes(material)
   826	            clause = by_position.get(p.position)
   827	            self._unknown_clauses(p, clause, getattr(clauses, "setup_pool", None),
   828	                                  getattr(clauses, "project_bonus", None))
   829	            extra = ({"discount_scope": clause.discount_scope, "setup_fee": clause.setup_fee,
   830	                      "packaging": clause.packaging, "commitment": clause.commitment} if clause
   831	                     else {"setup_fee": getattr(p, "setup_fee", Decimal(0))})
   832	            try:
   833	                positions.append(to_position_input(p.position, p.quantity, p.unit, self.requirements[req_id],
   834	                                                   material, **extra))
   835	            except calc.CalcError as error:
   836	                problems.append(f"position {p.position}: {error}")
   837	                positions.append(to_position_input(p.position, p.quantity, p.unit, self.requirements[req_id], None,
   838	                                                   **extra) if material is None else
   839	                                 calc.PositionInput(position=p.position, quantity=p.quantity,
   840	                                                    unit=p.unit if isinstance(p.unit, calc.Unit) else calc.parse_unit(p.unit),
   841	                                                    pieces_per_set=self.requirements[req_id].pieces_per_set, **extra))
   842	        bid = calc.BidInput(tender_reference=self.reference, scenario_date=self.scenario_stamp, positions=positions,
   843	                            approval=getattr(clauses, "approval", None) or getattr(self.mail_facts, "approval", None),
   844	                            fx_rates=getattr(clauses, "fx_rates", None) or getattr(self.mail_facts, "fx_rates", {}) or {},
   845	                            metal_indices=getattr(clauses, "metal_indices", None)
   846	                            or getattr(self.mail_facts, "metal_indices", {}) or {},
   847	                            setup_pool=getattr(clauses, "setup_pool", None),
   848	                            project_bonus=getattr(clauses, "project_bonus", None))
   849	        return bid, problems
   850	
   851	    def fallback_answer(self) -> dict:
   852	        """
   853	        A bid with every position omitted: the reference, the decision, the discount of an approval that was read
   854	        (a conditional one only when no positions exist to meet its threshold means 0, rule 16) and total 0.
   855	        """
   856	        try:
   857	            approval = getattr(self.mail_facts, "approval", None)
   858	            bid = calc.BidInput(tender_reference=self.reference, scenario_date=self.scenario_stamp, positions=[],
   859	                                approval=approval if isinstance(approval, calc.Approval) else None)
   860	            return calc.calculate(bid).answer()
   861	        except Exception:
   862	            return {"tender_reference": self.reference, "decision": "bid", "currency": "EUR",
   863	                    "discount_percent": 0.0, "positions": [], "total_net": 0.0}
   864	
   865	    async def run(self) -> tuple[dict | None, calc.BidResult | None]:
   866	        """Research, verify, calculate: the answer dict for the bid form. Positions that are not complete are
   867	        omitted; with none complete it is still a bid with reference, decision and discount."""
   868	        await self.research()
   869	        # The deadline guard after research: each step runs only in the time the bid form leaves it.
   870	        if self.form_left() > 60:
   871	            await self._bounded(self.verify(), "verify")
   872	        await self._bounded(self.select_materials(), "select")
   873	        bid, problems = self.build_bid()
   874	        self.trace.event("calc", "input", positions=[p.position for p in bid.positions], problems=problems)
   875	        if not bid.positions:
   876	            self.board.problem("calc", "no position could be built; the bid goes in with every position omitted")
   877	        result, blank, calc_problems = safe_calculate(bid)
   878	        for position, fields in self.blank_hints.items():
   879	            blank.setdefault(position, set()).update(fields)
   880	        problems += calc_problems
   881	        if result is None:  # still a bid: reference, decision and discount score without positions
   882	            answer = self.fallback_answer()
   883	            self.trace.event("calc", "answer", answer=answer, problems=problems, fallback=True)
   884	            return answer, None
   885	        # The check can only turn a bid with missing materials into no_bid; calc never returns such a bid today,
   886	        # so it is asked only then and costs the bid form no time otherwise.
   887	        disputable = result.decision == "bid" and bool(result.missing_materials)
   888	        check = None if self.form_left() < 30 or not disputable else await confirm_decision(
   889	            result.decision, self.board.summary() + "\n\nProblems:\n" + "\n".join(self.board.problems + problems),

   891	        if check is not None and not check.agrees:
   892	            self.trace.event("verify", "decision_disputed", proposed=result.decision, wanted=check.decision,
   893	                             reason=check.reason)
   894	        if check is not None and check.decision == "no_bid" and result.decision == "bid" and result.missing_materials:

   896	        answer = answer_from(result, blank)
   897	        self.trace.event("calc", "answer", answer=answer, problems=problems, blank={k: sorted(v) for k, v in blank.items()})

# Answers and scoring

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

Each challenge defines its answer format and how quality is scored; the platform measures cost and time and
ranks everyone the same way. Test runs, scored submissions and the scouting logins use the public dataset (the
websites as you see them, with scenario `public-1`), and the leaderboard ranks those results. The correct answer
isn't published; your system has to work it out from the websites. When the hackathon ends, a [final run](#final-run)
on a private dataset weighs most when we pick the [winners](#winners).

## Per run

- **Quality** (0 to 100): how right the answer is, by the challenge's scorer.
- **Eligible:** whether the answer meets the challenge's mandatory criteria. For RFQ: the right tender reference;
  a wrong decision (bid or no_bid) costs quality points instead.
- **Cost:** the run's LLM usage, priced per model, in USD.
- **Time:** from the start of your run command to your accepted answer.

A malformed answer is rejected with a `400` and does not end the run. A well-formed answer is final, even if it
is wrong. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.

## Leaderboard

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset and is scored; one run per submission
keeps your model bill down. A submission appears once its run has finished and review is passed; reviewer flags await organizer approval. Each team is ranked by its best
complete submission. The API reports them in its `median_*` fields; with one run per submission, that is
the run's own value.

1. Eligible before ineligible.
2. Higher quality.
3. Lower cost × time: the submission's cost in USD times its time, with cost counted as at least $0.01 and time
   as at least 1 second. Cost and time weigh the same: halving your model bill counts as much as halving your run
   time, and among free runs the faster one wins.
4. The submission ID, when everything above is equal.

On the leaderboard's plot, each team is a dot, quality against cost or time; the dotted line is the Pareto front,
the teams no other eligible team beats on both.

Test runs and scored runs on the public scenario `public-1` show your team the points for each part of the answer,
never the expected values. Runs on the private dataset show quality, eligibility, cost and time without a breakdown.

## Final run

When the hackathon ends, the organizers run every team's latest submission that passed review (organizers resolve outstanding reviewer flags before the final run starts; rejected ones don't count) once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it, and each run's brief states the bid rules. It ranks in the same order as above. Build an agent that works the
answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario.

## Winners

We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order:

1. Performance on the private dataset (the final run).
2. Performance on the public dataset (the leaderboard).
3. The elegance of the system.

It is the latest submission, not the best one: your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard; your
latest one that passed review goes into the final run. The final run's results stay with the organizers until they
publish them. Then the leaderboard shows the final results, tagged "Private dataset · final", with each team's
public-dataset result and its change in rank beside them, and the public-dataset board stays at `$API/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public` (Markdown:
`leaderboard.md?dataset=public`; API: `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/leaderboard?dataset=public`).

## RFQ scoring

The brief states the calculation rules. Each position has four optional fields that earn independent points:
`base_unit_price` (the EUR scale price per piece before discount), `surcharge_per_unit` (material surcharge plus
ordinary and allocated setup cost per piece, before discount), `packaging_per_unit`, and `rebate_total` (the
project-bonus credit for the **entire position**). Leave a field blank if unanswered; enter zero for a known zero.
The same calculation rules and answer format apply to the public and private datasets. You can also explicitly
omit unfinished positions in the form; completed fields retain their credit. You must sign and submit to score.

| Part (a bid) | Points |
| --- | --- |
| Decision | 5 |
| Tender reference | 5 |
| Discount percent | 5 |
| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (when present) | 5 |
| Dated metal-index check (when present) | 5 |
| Positions (split evenly): material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus 10 %, unit price 10 %, lead time 10 % | 75 minus the checks above |


For a no_bid case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, a total of 0 15. A wrong decision costs its
points but leaves the other fields their credit.

Money is compared to the cent. Positions are matched by their position number; extra or duplicate positions cost
one position's share each.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission on the private set. The default is one attempt.
Before the final run starts, opt in to **Best of 3** on your team page or run
`atira final --best-of 3` (`--best-of 1` opts out). `atira status` shows the choice.
When the final run starts, each team's choice is fixed, including teams still in review.
Opted-in teams get up to three attempts on the same private scenario(s). Your **single best complete attempt**
counts: eligible first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time, with the leaderboard's usual floors.
It is not an average, and a failed attempt does not outweigh a better successful one.
Every attempt is kept. Your team sees its own attempts' logs (private values masked) and, once the organizers publish the final, the results.
Calls using your own model keys can cost up to **3×**. The public leaderboard remains one run per submission
on the public scenario. Review, flags and disqualification work as for any submission.

Flagged results are hidden from the public leaderboard by default. **Show flagged** on the page (or `?flagged=1` on
the leaderboard API) lists them beside the approved ones, tagged "flagged: waiting for an organizer" and without a
rank, so showing them does not change other ranks. An organizer pass makes a flagged result count normally.

  their attributes; per hit a worker opens the views with status, stock, lead times, carton size, masses, index

  reads them into a record. A model then chooses the material (thinking on); `evidence.check_choice` validates the

  in its own tab.

import contextlib
import inspect

import re
import time

from typing import TypeVar
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlparse

from playwright.async_api import BrowserContext, Page

    EffectiveRequirement,
    MaterialRecord,

    SpecRevision,

    parse_int,
    parse_mass_kg,
    parse_number,
    parse_pieces_per_set,

from tracing import Trace
from worker import run_worker, steps_for

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)

_REF = re.compile(r"\[e\d+ ")


def on_site(site: dict, url: str) -> str | None:
    """The absolute URL of a link target if it is on the site's own host (the goto tool's rule), else None."""

    return target if urlparse(target).netloc == urlparse(site["url"]).netloc else None


def _strip_refs(text: str) -> str:
    return _REF.sub("[", text)


def _read_settings(thinking: bool):

    90 s) in either mode, since the thinking-off default is tuned for short navigation steps."""

# Readers copy values from pages a worker chose, under a grounding check; thinking makes each call ~30 s instead of
# ~5 s for little gain there. Judgement calls (which revision governs) always think.
READ_THINKING = os.environ.get("RESEARCH_READ_THINKING", "0") == "1"

async def _grounded_read(output_type: type[T], instructions: str, prompt: str, source: str, *,
                         trace: Trace | None = None, name: str = "research", what: str = "") -> T:
    """One reader call: the model reports what `source` (the text it is shown) says; every value it returns must
    appear in that text, else it is told which ones do not and tries again. Traced with seconds and refusals."""
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=output_type, instructions=instructions,
                  model_settings=_read_settings(READ_THINKING), retries=3)
    refusals: list[str] = []

    @agent.output_validator
    def _grounded(out):
        missing = unseen_values(out.model_dump_json(), source)
        if missing:
            refusals.extend(missing[:10])
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(missing[:10])} are not in the text; copy values exactly from it.")
        return out

        return (await agent.run(prompt)).output

def same_revision(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Revision labels as reported may carry a word around the id ("Revision R-2" vs "R-2")."""
    a, b = " ".join(a.split()).casefold(), " ".join(b.split()).casefold()
    return bool(a and b) and (a == b or a in b or b in a)


def _worker_kwargs(**kwargs) -> dict:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- which website is which


class ResearchSites(BaseModel):
    spec_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website that holds the buyer's technical specification and "
                                       "its revisions")

                                      "times and price conditions")


async def research_sites(task: dict) -> ResearchSites:
    """Map the specification and ERP roles to siteIds from the brief (the private run renames and re-splits)."""
    ids = {s["siteId"] for s in task["access"]}
    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {s['siteId']}: {s['url']}" for s in task["access"])
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=ResearchSites, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=False), retries=3,
                  instructions="You read a task brief and say which website plays which part, using its siteIds.")

    @agent.output_validator
    def _known(out: ResearchSites) -> ResearchSites:
        if out.spec_site not in ids or out.erp_site not in ids:
            raise ModelRetry(f"spec_site and erp_site must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")

    return result.output


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tools that read what the model chose

_DOCUMENTS: dict[int, list[str]] = {}  # id(session) -> page texts read by read_document


def _common_edges(texts: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Lines shared at the start and at the end of every text (site chrome), to show them only once."""
    lines = [t.splitlines() for t in texts]
    if len(lines) < 2:
        return 0, 0
    head = 0
    while all(len(x) > head for x in lines) and len({x[head] for x in lines}) == 1:
        head += 1
    tail = 0
    while all(len(x) > head + tail for x in lines) and len({x[-1 - tail] for x in lines}) == 1:
        tail += 1
    return head, tail


_LINK = re.compile(r"-> (\S+?)\]")


async def open_pages(ctx: RunContext[Deps], paths: list[str]) -> str:
    """Read several pages of this website in one step, e.g. the tabs, sub-views or records of what you are
    investigating. Give link targets exactly as pages you have seen show them (at most 10). The texts come back
    without refs, followed by the links on them you have not opened yet; you end up on the last one
    (read_more(offset=0) shows its refs)."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    opened: set[str] = session.__dict__.setdefault("opened", set())  # link targets read in this session
    texts, names = [], []

    async def goto(target: str) -> str:
        async with session.lock:
            await session._goto(target)
            session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="open_pages", url=target)
            return await session.look()

    def landed_on(target: str) -> bool:
        landed, wanted = urlparse(session.page.url), urlparse(target)
        return (landed.path, landed.query) == (wanted.path, wanted.query)

    for path in list(dict.fromkeys(paths))[:10]:
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        rel = parsed.path + (f"?{parsed.query}" if parsed.query else "")
        if path not in session.seen and rel not in session.seen:
            texts.append("not opened: no page you have seen links there")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        target = urljoin(session.page.url, path)
        if urlparse(target).netloc != urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc:
            texts.append("not opened: not on this website")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        if target in opened:
            texts.append("already opened and kept for the reader")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        view = await goto(target)
        recover = getattr(session, "recover", None)
        if not landed_on(target) and recover is not None:  # the session dropped: one tab gets past the gate
            await recover()
            view = await goto(target)
        if not landed_on(target):
            texts.append(f"did not open: the site showed {session.page.url} instead (handle that page, then open "
                         f"this view again)\n" + _strip_refs(view.split("\n\n", 1)[-1])[:3000])
            names.append(path)
            continue
        opened.add(target)
        texts.append(_strip_refs(view.split("\n\n", 1)[-1])[:8000])
        names.append(path)

    def was_opened(text: str) -> bool:
        return not text.startswith(("not opened", "did not open", "already opened"))

    head, tail = _common_edges([t for t in texts if was_opened(t)])
    out, more = [], {}
    for i, (name, text) in enumerate(zip(names, texts)):
        if was_opened(text):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            body = "\n".join(lines[head:len(lines) - tail]) if len(texts) > 1 else text  # not the site chrome
            for link in _LINK.findall(body):
                target = urljoin(session.page.url, link)
                if urlparse(target).netloc == urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc and target not in opened:
                    more.setdefault(link, None)
        if i and was_opened(text) and (head or tail):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            text = "\n".join(lines[head:len(lines) - tail]) + "\n[page frame as in the first page]"
        out.append(f"=== {name}\n{text}")
    if more:
        out.append("Links on these views you have not opened yet: " + " ".join(list(more)[:40]))
    return "\n\n".join(out)


def _control(view: str, ref: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    m = re.search(r"\[" + re.escape(ref) + r' (\w+) "([^"]*)"', view)
    return (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else None


async def _click(element) -> None:
    try:
        await element.click(timeout=5000)
    except Exception:
        await element.evaluate("e => e.click()")


async def read_document(ctx: RunContext[Deps], next_ref: str = "") -> str:
    """Read the whole document you have open: give the ref of its control that shows the next page or loads more
    (next_ref), and every page is read in turn and kept for extraction. Leave next_ref empty when the document has
    a single page. Call it while the document version you chose is open."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    pages = [session.view]
    control = _control(session.view, next_ref) if next_ref else None
    if next_ref and control is None:
        return f"No control {next_ref} in the current view; use a ref from the latest view."
    if control:
        role, label = control
        pattern = re.compile(r"\[(e\d+) " + re.escape(role) + r' "' + re.escape(label) + r'"(?![^\]]*disabled)')
        nth = [m.group(1) for m in pattern.finditer(session.view)].index(next_ref)
        seen = {_strip_refs(session.view)}
        for _ in range(40):
            refs = [m.group(1) for m in pattern.finditer(session.view)]
            if not refs:
                break
            await session.act("click", refs[min(nth, len(refs) - 1)], _click)
            text = _strip_refs(session.view)
            if text in seen:  # a slow site may still be loading the next page (a local run lost pages 3 to 5)
                await asyncio.sleep(PAGE_WAIT)
                await session.settle()
                await session.look()
                text = _strip_refs(session.view)
            if text in seen:  # past the end some sites repeat the last page
                break
            seen.add(text)
            pages.append(session.view)
    # "load more" pages contain the earlier ones: keep only pages no later page contains
    stripped = [_strip_refs(p) for p in pages]
    keep = [p for i, p in enumerate(stripped) if not any(p in later for later in stripped[i + 1:])]
    _DOCUMENTS[id(session)] = keep
    session.trace.event(session.name, "read_document", pages=len(pages), kept=len(keep),
                        chars=sum(len(p) for p in keep))
    return (f"Read {len(pages)} views of the document ({len(keep)} distinct, {sum(len(p) for p in keep)} "
            f"characters); they are kept for extraction. Return your result now.\n\n" + await session.look())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- specification


class RevisionSeen(BaseModel):
    revision: str = Field(description="Revision identifier as shown")
    status: str = Field(description="Its status as shown, including statuses only visible in tooltips")


class RevisionHistory(BaseModel):
    document: str = Field(description="The specification document's number or title as shown")
    revisions: list[RevisionSeen] = Field(description="Every revision the document's history lists")


class CurrentRevision(BaseModel):
    revision: str = Field(description="The revision the site marks as currently valid, exactly as shown")
    why: str = Field(description="What on the page marks it as current, in a few words")


class Opened(BaseModel):
    done: bool = Field(description="True once read_document has read the requested revision")


class RequirementSeen(BaseModel):
    requirement_id: str = Field(description="The requirement's reference as shown")
    bore: str = Field(description="Bore in mm, exactly as shown")
    stroke: str = Field(description="Stroke (travel) in mm, exactly as shown")
    pressure: str = Field(description="Operating pressure in bar, exactly as shown")
    mounting: str = Field(description="Mounting type as written")
    certification: str = Field(description="Required certification as written, or the words saying none is "
                                           "required")
    catalog_group: str = Field(description="The Kataloggruppe (catalogue group code) named for the ERP search")
    pieces_per_set: str = Field("", description="How many pieces one set (Satz) holds, if the text defines a set "
                                                 "(the piece count only, e.g. '4' for '1 set = 4 pieces'), else ''")
    stroke_is_usable_travel: bool = Field(description="True if the stroke is stated as usable travel (nutzbarer "
                                                      "Weg) to which a reserve must be added for the ERP stroke")
    reserve_key: str = Field("", description="The key of that end reserve, if named, else ''")
    conflict: str = Field("", description="Only if the table and the full wording disagree: how; else ''")


class SpecPage(BaseModel):
    revision_shown: str = Field(description="The revision this page belongs to, as shown on it, or ''")
    requirements: list[RequirementSeen]


FIND_SPEC_GOAL = """\
Find the buyer's technical specification document for the tender in the context, open its revision history and
return the revisions it lists. Steps: open the website's document register or list; read it with collect (all its
pages in one step) and pick the specification by the tender's reference or subject; open that document. If the
site asks for a confirmation before releasing documents, choose the option that gives access to the binding
documents (archive copies or previews are not the governing ones) and copy any number it asks you to transfer
exactly. On the document, open its revision history (it may be collapsed behind a control) and read it with collect;
return every revision it lists with its status as shown (statuses may only be visible in tooltips), so the revision
marked as currently valid can be identified. Once the revision history shows, return at once."""

CHOOSE_REVISION = """\
You decide which revision of a buyer's specification governs a bid: the one the document marks as currently valid
(in whatever words the site uses), never one marked as superseded, replaced or withdrawn. Documents may list or open the
oldest revision first, and dates may be written in different orders, so go by the marked status; use dates only if
no status marks one revision as current."""

OPEN_REVISION_GOAL = """\
Open the requirements of revision {revision} of the specification document you have open (not another revision).
Once its first page of requirements shows, call read_document with the ref of the control that shows the next page
or loads more (leave it empty if everything is on one page), so that all its requirements are read; then return."""

EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You extract requirements from one page of a technical specification exactly as written. Copy numbers as shown
including any locale tag next to them; never convert, compute or guess. Each requirement may appear both as
a table row and in its full original wording (which wins if they differ). Report only requirements that this page
shows; return an empty list if it shows none."""


async def _extract_page(text: str, document: str, revision: str, context: str, trace: Trace | None,
                        name: str) -> SpecPage | None:
    prompt = f"Document {document}, revision {revision} (the current one).\nContext: {context}\n\nPage:\n{text}"
    try:
        return await _grounded_read(SpecPage, EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS, prompt, text, trace=trace, name=name,
                                    what="spec page")
    except Exception as error:  # one bad page must not sink the rest
        print(f"[research] spec page extraction failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}", flush=True)
        return None


async def _choose_revision(history: RevisionHistory, view: str, context: str) -> CurrentRevision | None:
    ids = {r.revision.strip() for r in history.revisions}
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=CurrentRevision, instructions=CHOOSE_REVISION,
                  model_settings=_read_settings(True), retries=3)

    @agent.output_validator
    def _listed(out: CurrentRevision) -> CurrentRevision:
        if not any(same_revision(out.revision, i) for i in ids):
            raise ModelRetry(f"Choose one of the listed revisions: {sorted(ids)}")
        return out

    listing = "\n".join(f"- {r.revision}: {r.status}" for r in history.revisions)
    prompt = (f"{context}\n\nDocument: {history.document}\nRevisions as reported:\n{listing}\n\n"
              f"The revision history page:\n{_strip_refs(view)[:12000]}")
    try:
        return (await agent.run(prompt)).output
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"[research] revision choice failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}", flush=True)
        return None

    opened: set[str] = session.__dict__.setdefault("opened", set())  # link targets read in this session
    texts, names = [], []

    async def goto(target: str) -> str:
        async with session.lock:
            await session._goto(target)
            session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="open_pages", url=target)
            return await session.look()

    def landed_on(target: str) -> bool:
        landed, wanted = urlparse(session.page.url), urlparse(target)
        return (landed.path, landed.query) == (wanted.path, wanted.query)

    for path in list(dict.fromkeys(paths))[:10]:
        parsed = urlparse(path)
        rel = parsed.path + (f"?{parsed.query}" if parsed.query else "")
        if path not in session.seen and rel not in session.seen:
            texts.append("not opened: no page you have seen links there")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        target = urljoin(session.page.url, path)
        if urlparse(target).netloc != urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc:
            texts.append("not opened: not on this website")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        if target in opened:
            texts.append("already opened and kept for the reader")
            names.append(path)
            continue
        view = await goto(target)
        recover = getattr(session, "recover", None)
        if not landed_on(target) and recover is not None:  # the session dropped: one tab gets past the gate
            await recover()
            view = await goto(target)
        if not landed_on(target):
            texts.append(f"did not open: the site showed {session.page.url} instead (handle that page, then open "
                         f"this view again)\n" + _strip_refs(view.split("\n\n", 1)[-1])[:3000])
            names.append(path)
            continue
        opened.add(target)
        texts.append(_strip_refs(view.split("\n\n", 1)[-1])[:8000])
        names.append(path)

    def was_opened(text: str) -> bool:
        return not text.startswith(("not opened", "did not open", "already opened"))

    head, tail = _common_edges([t for t in texts if was_opened(t)])
    out, more = [], {}
    for i, (name, text) in enumerate(zip(names, texts)):
        if was_opened(text):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            body = "\n".join(lines[head:len(lines) - tail]) if len(texts) > 1 else text  # not the site chrome
            for link in _LINK.findall(body):
                target = urljoin(session.page.url, link)
                if urlparse(target).netloc == urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc and target not in opened:
                    more.setdefault(link, None)
        if i and was_opened(text) and (head or tail):
            lines = text.splitlines()
            text = "\n".join(lines[head:len(lines) - tail]) + "\n[page frame as in the first page]"
        out.append(f"=== {name}\n{text}")
    if more:
        out.append("Links on these views you have not opened yet: " + " ".join(list(more)[:40]))
    return "\n\n".join(out)


def _control(view: str, ref: str) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    m = re.search(r"\[" + re.escape(ref) + r' (\w+) "([^"]*)"', view)
    return (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else None


async def _click(element) -> None:
    try:
        await element.click(timeout=5000)
    except Exception:
        await element.evaluate("e => e.click()")


async def read_document(ctx: RunContext[Deps], next_ref: str = "") -> str:
    """Read the whole document you have open: give the ref of its control that shows the next page or loads more
    (next_ref), and every page is read in turn and kept for extraction. Leave next_ref empty when the document has
    a single page. Call it while the document version you chose is open."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    pages = [session.view]
    control = _control(session.view, next_ref) if next_ref else None
    if next_ref and control is None:
        return f"No control {next_ref} in the current view; use a ref from the latest view."
    if control:
        role, label = control
        pattern = re.compile(r"\[(e\d+) " + re.escape(role) + r' "' + re.escape(label) + r'"(?![^\]]*disabled)')
        nth = [m.group(1) for m in pattern.finditer(session.view)].index(next_ref)
        seen = {_strip_refs(session.view)}
        for _ in range(40):
            refs = [m.group(1) for m in pattern.finditer(session.view)]
            if not refs:
                break
            await session.act("click", refs[min(nth, len(refs) - 1)], _click)
            text = _strip_refs(session.view)
            if text in seen:  # a slow site may still be loading the next page (a local run lost pages 3 to 5)
                await asyncio.sleep(PAGE_WAIT)
                await session.settle()
                await session.look()
                text = _strip_refs(session.view)
            if text in seen:  # past the end some sites repeat the last page
                break
            seen.add(text)
            pages.append(session.view)
    # "load more" pages contain the earlier ones: keep only pages no later page contains
    stripped = [_strip_refs(p) for p in pages]
    keep = [p for i, p in enumerate(stripped) if not any(p in later for later in stripped[i + 1:])]
    _DOCUMENTS[id(session)] = keep
    session.trace.event(session.name, "read_document", pages=len(pages), kept=len(keep),
                        chars=sum(len(p) for p in keep))
    return (f"Read {len(pages)} views of the document ({len(keep)} distinct, {sum(len(p) for p in keep)} "
            f"characters); they are kept for extraction. Return your result now.\n\n" + await session.look())

FIND_SPEC_GOAL = """\
Find the buyer's technical specification document for the tender in the context, open its revision history and
return the revisions it lists. Steps: open the website's document register or list; read it with collect (all its
pages in one step) and pick the specification by the tender's reference or subject; open that document. If the
site asks for a confirmation before releasing documents, choose the option that gives access to the binding
documents (archive copies or previews are not the governing ones) and copy any number it asks you to transfer
exactly. On the document, open its revision history (it may be collapsed behind a control) and read it with collect;
return every revision it lists with its status as shown (statuses may only be visible in tooltips), so the revision
marked as currently valid can be identified. Once the revision history shows, return at once."""

CHOOSE_REVISION = """\
You decide which revision of a buyer's specification governs a bid: the one the document marks as currently valid
(in whatever words the site uses), never one marked as superseded, replaced or withdrawn. Documents may list or open the
oldest revision first, and dates may be written in different orders, so go by the marked status; use dates only if
no status marks one revision as current."""

OPEN_REVISION_GOAL = """\
Open the requirements of revision {revision} of the specification document you have open (not another revision).
Once its first page of requirements shows, call read_document with the ref of the control that shows the next page
or loads more (leave it empty if everything is on one page), so that all its requirements are read; then return."""

EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You extract requirements from one page of a technical specification exactly as written. Copy numbers as shown
including any locale tag next to them; never convert, compute or guess. Each requirement may appear both as
a table row and in its full original wording (which wins if they differ). Report only requirements that this page
shows; return an empty list if it shows none."""


async def _extract_page(text: str, document: str, revision: str, context: str, trace: Trace | None,
                        name: str) -> SpecPage | None:
    prompt = f"Document {document}, revision {revision} (the current one).\nContext: {context}\n\nPage:\n{text}"
    try:
        return await _grounded_read(SpecPage, EXTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS, prompt, text, trace=trace, name=name,
                                    what="spec page")
    except Exception as error:  # one bad page must not sink the rest
        print(f"[research] spec page extraction failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}", flush=True)
        return None


async def _choose_revision(history: RevisionHistory, view: str, context: str) -> CurrentRevision | None:
    ids = {r.revision.strip() for r in history.revisions}
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=CurrentRevision, instructions=CHOOSE_REVISION,
                  model_settings=_read_settings(True), retries=3)

    @agent.output_validator
    def _listed(out: CurrentRevision) -> CurrentRevision:
        if not any(same_revision(out.revision, i) for i in ids):
            raise ModelRetry(f"Choose one of the listed revisions: {sorted(ids)}")
        return out

    listing = "\n".join(f"- {r.revision}: {r.status}" for r in history.revisions)
    prompt = (f"{context}\n\nDocument: {history.document}\nRevisions as reported:\n{listing}\n\n"
              f"The revision history page:\n{_strip_refs(view)[:12000]}")
    try:
        return (await agent.run(prompt)).output
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"[research] revision choice failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}", flush=True)
        return None

content.content:
SALVAGE_VIEWS = 12  # requirement pages read from what the open-revision worker showed, beyond read_document

SALVAGE_HISTORY = """\
You read the page a browsing worker ended on. If it shows the revision history of a specification document (a list
of its revisions with their statuses, which may only be visible in tooltips), report the document and every revision
with its status exactly as shown. If it shows no revision list, return an empty list of revisions."""


async def _salvage_history(session: SiteSession, context: str) -> RevisionHistory | None:
    """The revisions on the page a stopped navigator ended on (one grounded reader call), or None."""
    text = _strip_refs(session.view or "")
    if not text.strip():
        return None
    try:
        history = await _grounded_read(RevisionHistory, SALVAGE_HISTORY, f"{context}\n\nPage:\n{text[:16000]}", text,
                                       trace=session.trace, name=session.name, what="revision history salvage")
    except Exception as error:
        session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_salvage_failed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
        return None
    return history if history.revisions else None


def _record_views(session: SiteSession) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every distinct page text the session shows, latest last (a document viewer may page inside one URL)."""
    views: dict[str, str] = {}
    look = session.look

    async def recording_look(offset: int = 0, **options) -> str:
        out = await look(offset, **options)
        if offset == 0:
            text = _strip_refs(session.view)
            key = f"{session.page.url}#{hash(text)}"
            views.pop(key, None)
            views[key] = text
        return out

    session.look = recording_look  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    return views


def _pieces_per_set(text: str) -> int | None:
    """None when the spec gives no set size or words it unclearly (a set position is then left out, not mispriced)."""
    try:
        return parse_pieces_per_set(text) if text.strip() else None
    except ParseError:
        return None


def _parse_requirement(seen: RequirementSeen, revision: str) -> Requirement:
    return Requirement(
        requirement_id=seen.requirement_id.strip(), revision=revision, bore=parse_number(seen.bore),
        stroke=parse_number(seen.stroke), pressure=parse_number(seen.pressure), mounting=seen.mounting.strip(),
        certification=seen.certification.strip(), catalog_group=seen.catalog_group.strip(),
        pieces_per_set=_pieces_per_set(seen.pieces_per_set),
        stroke_is_usable=seen.stroke_is_usable_travel, reserve_key=seen.reserve_key.strip() or None,
        raw={k: str(v) for k, v in seen.model_dump().items()})


async def research_spec(session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, *, context: str = "",
                        deadline: float | None = None, on_requirement=None, on_revision=None,
                        thinking: bool = False, max_steps: int = 25) -> SpecResult:
    """
    The current specification revision's requirements: a worker finds the document and its revision history
    (navigation, thinking off), a model decides the current revision (thinking on), the worker opens it and pages
    through it, and a model extracts each page (thinking on, in parallel).

    `on_revision()` runs once the governing revision is chosen (e.g. to warm up the ERP), `on_requirement(req)` as
    soon as each requirement is parsed, so ERP research can start before the last page is read. `thinking`
    turns thinking on for finding the document, `max_steps` bounds that navigation (more while time is ample). A
    navigator that stops early still gets its revisions read from the page it ended on, and requirement pages it
    showed are read even when read_document was not used on them (partial requirements beat none).
    """
    started = time.monotonic()
    result = SpecResult()
    goal_context = f"Tender reference: {briefing.tender_reference}\n{context}".strip()

    def finish(problem: str | None = None) -> SpecResult:
        if problem:
            result.problems.append(problem)
        result.seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
        session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_done", seconds=result.seconds, revision=result.current_revision,
                            requirements=[r.requirement_id for r in result.requirements], problems=result.problems)
        return result

    from site_tools import collect  # one step for a document register or a revision list
    views = _record_views(session)
    history, _ = await run_worker(session, FIND_SPEC_GOAL, RevisionHistory, context=goal_context, deadline=deadline,
                                  max_steps=steps_for(max_steps, deadline, most=1.4), tools=(collect,),
                                  **_worker_kwargs(notes=False, thinking=thinking))
    if history is None or not history.revisions:
        # The navigator ran out of steps or time, often while already on the history: read the revisions from the
        # page it ended on before giving up.
        history = await _salvage_history(session, goal_context)
        if history is None:
            return finish("no revision history found")
        session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_salvaged", revisions=[r.revision for r in history.revisions])
    result.document = history.document
    result.revisions = [SpecRevision(revision=r.revision, status_shown=r.status) for r in history.revisions]
    choice = await _choose_revision(history, session.view, goal_context)
    if choice is None:
        return finish("no current revision chosen")
    result.current_revision = choice.revision.strip()
    session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_revision", revision=result.current_revision, why=choice.why)
    if on_revision:
        on_revision()

    views.clear()  # from here on: the pages shown while the revision is opened
    pages: list[str] = []
    for _ in range(2):
        await run_worker(session, OPEN_REVISION_GOAL.format(revision=result.current_revision), Opened,
                         context=goal_context, deadline=deadline, max_steps=12, tools=(read_document,),
                         **_worker_kwargs(notes=False, grounded=False))
        pages = _DOCUMENTS.pop(id(session), [])
        if pages:
            break
    # Requirement pages the worker showed but read_document did not read (it stopped midway, or paged only part of
    # the document) are read too; they count only when the page itself shows the chosen revision, and only for
    # requirements the read pages do not have.
    extra = [v for v in list(views.values())[-SALVAGE_VIEWS:] if not any(v in p or p in v for p in pages)]
    if not pages and not extra:
        return finish(f"revision {result.current_revision} could not be read")
    session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_extract", pages=len(pages), salvage=len(extra))
    by_id: dict[str, Requirement] = {}
    streamed: set[str] = set()

    def stream(page: SpecPage | None, salvage: bool) -> None:
        if page is None or on_requirement is None:
            return
        shown = page.revision_shown.strip()
        if (shown and not same_revision(shown, result.current_revision)) or (salvage and not shown):
            return
        for seen in page.requirements:
            try:
                req = _parse_requirement(seen, result.current_revision)
            except ParseError:
                continue
            if req.requirement_id not in streamed:
                streamed.add(req.requirement_id)
                on_requirement(req)

    async def extract(text: str, salvage: bool = False) -> SpecPage | None:
        page = await _extract_page(text, history.document, result.current_revision, goal_context, session.trace,
                                   session.name)
        if not salvage:
            stream(page, False)
        return page

    extracted = await asyncio.gather(*(extract(p) for p in pages), *(extract(v, True) for v in extra))
    for i, page in enumerate(extracted):
        salvage = i >= len(pages)
        if salvage:  # after every read page, so a read page's requirement always wins
            stream(page, True)
        if page is None:
            if not salvage:
                result.problems.append("a document page could not be extracted")
            continue
        if page.revision_shown and not same_revision(page.revision_shown, result.current_revision):
            if not salvage:
                result.problems.append(f"a page shows revision {page.revision_shown}, not {result.current_revision}")
            continue
        if salvage and not page.revision_shown.strip():
            continue
        for seen in page.requirements:
            try:
                req = _parse_requirement(seen, result.current_revision)
            except ParseError as error:
                result.problems.append(f"{seen.requirement_id}: {error}")
                continue
            if seen.conflict:
                result.problems.append(f"{req.requirement_id}: {seen.conflict}")
            if req.requirement_id in by_id and by_id[req.requirement_id].raw != req.raw and not salvage:
                result.problems.append(f"{req.requirement_id} read differently on two pages")
            by_id.setdefault(req.requirement_id, req)
    result.requirements = sorted(by_id.values(), key=lambda r: calc.position_key(r.requirement_id))
    return finish()

def _want(req: EffectiveRequirement) -> str:
    stroke = f"stroke {req.stroke} mm" if req.stroke is not None else "stroke not yet known (ignore it)"
    return (f"bore {req.bore} mm, {stroke}, pressure {req.pressure} bar, mounting {req.mounting}, certification "
            f"{req.certification}")


def _num(text: str) -> Decimal | None:
    try:
        return parse_number(text) if text and text.strip() else None
    except ParseError:
        return None


def _material_record(seen: MaterialSeen) -> MaterialRecord:
    problems: list[str] = []

    def get(fn, text, *args):
        if not text or not str(text).strip():
            return None
        try:
            return fn(text, *args)
        except (ParseError, ValueError) as error:
            problems.append(str(error))
            return None

    conditions = []
    for c in seen.conditions:
        fmt = number_format(c.number_format) if c.number_format else None
        if not c.scales:
            problems.append(f"condition {c.valid_from}..{c.valid_to}: scales not read")
            continue
        try:
            scales = [calc.PriceScale(min_quantity=parse_int(s.min_quantity, fmt),
                                      price=parse_number(s.price, fmt)) for s in c.scales]
            conditions.append(calc.PriceCondition(

def _corpus(views: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """The kept views as one text, site chrome shown once."""
    texts = list(views.values())
    head, tail = _common_edges(texts)
    parts = []
    for i, (url, text) in enumerate(views.items()):
        lines = text.splitlines()
        if i and (head or tail):

def steps(until: float | None, floor: int, cap: int) -> int:
    """A worker's step limit: what the time until `until` allows at about STEP_SECONDS a step, between `floor`
    and `cap` (the cap only stops loops; the deadline stops the worker anyway)."""
    if until is None:
        return cap
    return int(max(floor, min(cap, (until - time.monotonic()) / STEP_SECONDS)))

class Erp:
    """
    The ERP website: one signed-in context and a few reused tabs, so requirements and materials run in parallel.

    The ERP drops its session after some idle minutes and when several tabs sign in at once. Sign-ins are therefore
    serialised over the tabs, and a tab that lands somewhere other than the view it asked for (a sign-in, an entry
    gate) gets one model worker past the gate (`recover`, one tab at a time) and opens its view again.
    """

    def __init__(self, site: dict, context: BrowserContext, trace: Trace, deadline: float | None = None):
        self.site, self.context, self.trace, self.deadline = site, context, trace, deadline
        self.ready: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self.materials: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        self.tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}
        # a few tabs at once: every tab is one more page load on a site that slows down under load
        self.tabs = asyncio.Semaphore(int(os.environ.get("ERP_TABS", "6")))
        self.idle_pages: list[Page] = []  # open tabs a finished worker left, reused instead of a fresh start
        self.opening = asyncio.Lock()  # fresh tabs sign in one after another
        self.signin = asyncio.Lock()  # one sign-in at a time
        self.signins = 0
        self.checking = asyncio.Lock()  # one idle check at a time
        self.gate = asyncio.Lock()  # one tab gets past an entry gate at a time
        self.passes = 0  # gates passed; a tab that waited for another one's pass just opens its view again
        self.gate_paths: set[str] = set()  # paths of the sign-in / notice gates seen
        self.home = ""  # the path the start address lands on while signed in and past the gate
        self.busy = 0  # workers using the ERP now
        self.active_at = 0.0  # last time a worker used it
        self.idle_limit = float(os.environ.get("ERP_IDLE_SECONDS", "120"))  # the ERP drops idle sessions
        self.partial: dict[str, RequirementResearch] = {}  # requirement -> research whose search has finished

async def research_spec(session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, *, context: str = "",
                        deadline: float | None = None, on_requirement=None, on_revision=None,
                        thinking: bool = False, max_steps: int = 25) -> SpecResult:
    """
    The current specification revision's requirements: a worker finds the document and its revision history
    (navigation, thinking off), a model decides the current revision (thinking on), the worker opens it and pages
    through it, and a model extracts each page (thinking on, in parallel).

    `on_revision()` runs once the governing revision is chosen (e.g. to warm up the ERP), `on_requirement(req)` as
    soon as each requirement is parsed, so ERP research can start before the last page is read. `thinking`
    turns thinking on for finding the document, `max_steps` bounds that navigation (more while time is ample). A
    navigator that stops early still gets its revisions read from the page it ended on, and requirement pages it
    showed are read even when read_document was not used on them (partial requirements beat none).
    """
    started = time.monotonic()
    result = SpecResult()
    goal_context = f"Tender reference: {briefing.tender_reference}\n{context}".strip()

    def finish(problem: str | None = None) -> SpecResult:
        if problem:
            result.problems.append(problem)
        result.seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
        session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_done", seconds=result.seconds, revision=result.current_revision,
                            requirements=[r.requirement_id for r in result.requirements], problems=result.problems)
        return result

    from site_tools import collect  # one step for a document register or a revision list
    views = _record_views(session)
    history, _ = await run_worker(session, FIND_SPEC_GOAL, RevisionHistory, context=goal_context, deadline=deadline,
                                  max_steps=steps_for(max_steps, deadline, most=1.4), tools=(collect,),
                                  **_worker_kwargs(notes=False, thinking=thinking))
    if history is None or not history.revisions:
        # The navigator ran out of steps or time, often while already on the history: read the revisions from the
        # page it ended on before giving up.
        history = await _salvage_history(session, goal_context)
        if history is None:
            return finish("no revision history found")
        session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_salvaged", revisions=[r.revision for r in history.revisions])
    result.document = history.document
    result.revisions = [SpecRevision(revision=r.revision, status_shown=r.status) for r in history.revisions]
    choice = await _choose_revision(history, session.view, goal_context)
    if choice is None:
        return finish("no current revision chosen")
    result.current_revision = choice.revision.strip()
    session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_revision", revision=result.current_revision, why=choice.why)
    if on_revision:
        on_revision()

    views.clear()  # from here on: the pages shown while the revision is opened
    pages: list[str] = []
    for _ in range(2):
        await run_worker(session, OPEN_REVISION_GOAL.format(revision=result.current_revision), Opened,
                         context=goal_context, deadline=deadline, max_steps=12, tools=(read_document,),
                         **_worker_kwargs(notes=False, grounded=False))
        pages = _DOCUMENTS.pop(id(session), [])
        if pages:
            break
    # Requirement pages the worker showed but read_document did not read (it stopped midway, or paged only part of
    # the document) are read too; they count only when the page itself shows the chosen revision, and only for
    # requirements the read pages do not have.
    extra = [v for v in list(views.values())[-SALVAGE_VIEWS:] if not any(v in p or p in v for p in pages)]
    if not pages and not extra:
        return finish(f"revision {result.current_revision} could not be read")
    session.trace.event(session.name, "spec_extract", pages=len(pages), salvage=len(extra))
    by_id: dict[str, Requirement] = {}
    streamed: set[str] = set()

    def stream(page: SpecPage | None, salvage: bool) -> None:
        if page is None or on_requirement is None:
            return
        shown = page.revision_shown.strip()
        if (shown and not same_revision(shown, result.current_revision)) or (salvage and not shown):
            return
        for seen in page.requirements:
            try:
                req = _parse_requirement(seen, result.current_revision)
            except ParseError:
                continue
            if req.requirement_id not in streamed:
                streamed.add(req.requirement_id)
                on_requirement(req)

    async def extract(text: str, salvage: bool = False) -> SpecPage | None:
        page = await _extract_page(text, history.document, result.current_revision, goal_context, session.trace,
                                   session.name)
        if not salvage:
            stream(page, False)
        return page

    extracted = await asyncio.gather(*(extract(p) for p in pages), *(extract(v, True) for v in extra))
    for i, page in enumerate(extracted):
        salvage = i >= len(pages)
        if salvage:  # after every read page, so a read page's requirement always wins
            stream(page, True)
        if page is None:
            if not salvage:
                result.problems.append("a document page could not be extracted")
            continue
        if page.revision_shown and not same_revision(page.revision_shown, result.current_revision):
            if not salvage:
                result.problems.append(f"a page shows revision {page.revision_shown}, not {result.current_revision}")
            continue
        if salvage and not page.revision_shown.strip():
            continue
        for seen in page.requirements:
            try:
                req = _parse_requirement(seen, result.current_revision)
            except ParseError as error:
                result.problems.append(f"{seen.requirement_id}: {error}")
                continue
            if seen.conflict:
                result.problems.append(f"{req.requirement_id}: {seen.conflict}")
            if req.requirement_id in by_id and by_id[req.requirement_id].raw != req.raw and not salvage:
                result.problems.append(f"{req.requirement_id} read differently on two pages")
            by_id.setdefault(req.requirement_id, req)
    result.requirements = sorted(by_id.values(), key=lambda r: calc.position_key(r.requirement_id))
    return finish()
